Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. New York Governor Kathy Hochul says the woman who accused
members of a Cornell University fraternity of gang rape in 2024 was failed by those who were
obligated to protect her. In a Friday news conference, Hochul said she's now turning the

Barry. An energy department employee accused of providing support to the Iran-backed Houthi rebels
made his first court appearance Friday. Northwest Public Broadcasting's Eric Bengal has a report.
An FBI investigation into Ashton Hamid Elabudi began when he allegedly bought chemicals and
materials often used to make homemade explosives. The 51-year-old Richland, Washington resident
allegedly sought to help the Houthis, the Iran-backed paramilitary group that has taken control of much
of Yemen. The U.S. has designated the Houthis a foreign terrorist organization. Elabudi, who
worked for the U.S. Department of Energy as an electrical engineer, allegedly traveled to Yemen
without authorization. The FBI says Elabudi wanted to help the Houthis improve their communications
capabilities. A detention hearing is scheduled for next week. For NPR News, I'm Eric Bengal
in Walla Walla, Washington. The group of seven says they've reached agreement to release 100
million barrels of oil and fuel products. The deal will begin with large amounts of diesel
after those fuel prices hit record high prices in the U.S. Those surging prices are causing
problems for Republicans with about one month left before November's midterm elections.
Nine out of 10 school buses across the country meanwhile run on diesel fuel, which hit a new
record high price last month. Despite the dramatic jump, those buses have to keep on rolling.
Colorado Public Radio's Ray Salomon reports. The soaring cost of diesel fuel is hitting school
districts where it hurts right in the transportation budget. Nathan Reimer is transportation
director in the Jefferson County School District near Denver, Colorado. You know, I didn't budget
for a war in Iran to affect my diesel prices. But some school districts have alternative bus
fleets that run on electricity or fuels like propane, and they haven't been affected by high
diesel costs. Most of those districts got federal funding for these school buses from the 2021
infrastructure law. The Trump administration halted that program earlier this year,
calling it "a disaster of wasteful spending." For NPR News, I'm Ray Salomon in Boulder, Colorado.
Stocks finished up on Friday, and this is NPR News.
The Fertilizer's price index, a measure that directly affects food security, spiked when
the U.S. war in Iran shut down shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Prices have since eased,
but many farmers in sub-Saharan Africa are finding alternative solutions, Dury Baskaran reports.
Zambia once imported almost all of its fertilizer. Creating its own became a food security issue
after the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the U.S. war on Iran caused big price spikes.
Zambian farmers like Kanangwanulov have turned to Bokashi, a fermented compost method popularized
in Japan as a cheaper alternative to synthetic fertilizers. It was a game changer for us to be
honest. Zambia is also increasing its domestic fertilizer production to meet demand. Last week,
a Chinese-Zambian conglomerate announced it would build a $1.5 billion fertilizer plant.
Dury Baskaran, NPR News. North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile into the sea on
Saturday. South Korea's military says the launch took place on the northeastern coast. It's the
latest in a series of launches that have taken place as tensions have increased between the two
countries. Three South Korean soldiers were injured earlier this year by mine explosions
in the demilitarized zone between the countries, and the South blames the North for those blasts.
The NFL has suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York for six games. The suspension comes
following his arrest earlier this year in a prostitution sting in Ohio. He was also fined
$500,000 for violating the league's personal conduct policy. York has not attended any games
or league meetings so far this season. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from Schwab.
